messages:
OpsBot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT alert — Elevated 5xx rate for /v1/generate in us-east-1 (p95 latency stable). Paging Miguel Soto and Priya Narayanan. See incident runbook: https://confluence.redwood/incidents/llm-5xx-us-east-1
PagerDuty: Miguel Soto (primary) notified via SMS
Miguel Soto: on it. joining bridge now. any immediate customer visible errors?
Danielle Chen: seeing a spike in customer error dashboards, around ~14:12 UTC. Some responses failing with 'model unavailable' and 502s. tagging support for impact list.
Miguel Soto: thanks. quick check: rolling deploy to ded-ml-pool happened ~14:05 UTC? anyone on deploy?
Priya Narayanan: I kicked a canary earlier for kernel optimization to dedicated servers in us-east-1 at 14:03. I thought it was low risk, but could correlate. switching to read-only deploy notes.
Miguel Soto: Priya, can you pause rollout? if it’s related we should stop further canaries.
Priya Narayanan: pausing rollout now. command: 
```
kubectl -n inference rollout pause deployment/ded-ml-pool
```
Miguel Soto: verifying pool health. running quick query: 
```
redwoodctl cluster health --region us-east-1 --pool ded-ml-pool
```
oncall-monitor-bot: ded-ml-pool: 18/24 pods Ready, 6 CrashLoopBackOff; avg 5xx rate for /v1/generate = 7.2% over 5m
Danielle Chen: CrashLoopBackOff on a lot of pods — likely from new kernel changes. metrics show OOMs and repeated initialization failures.
Miguel Soto: ok — immediate mitigation: 1) scale down canary instances, 2) fallback routing to compatible model variant in other region if capacity allows, 3) open ticket and notify sales for impacted customers. Priya, can you scale canary down and roll back the kernel patch?
Priya Narayanan: scaling canaries down to 2. rolling back kernel patch to previous image now. command: 
```
kubectl -n inference set image deployment/ded-ml-pool ded-worker=redwood/ded-worker:release-2026-04-18
```
OpsBot: Action logged — rollback started by Priya Narayanan
Miguel Soto: I'll put a temporary routing rule to divert 10% of traffic to us-west-2 stable pool to reduce pressure.
Danielle Chen: I'm opening ticket for post-incident follow-up and customer impact tracking: TKT-4921. Adding initial summary + customer list.
Miguel Soto: thanks. for the handoff later: I'm primary until 15:30 UTC, Priya will be secondary for the remainder of this shift. After rollback completes, monitor 5xx for 15m and confirm.
Priya Narayanan: copy. I'll keep a watch for init errors and kernel logs. runbook pointer: https://runbooks.redwood/llm/rollback-guidance (see 'kernel-compat' section)
Miguel Soto: quick mitigations checklist: 
- paused rollout (done)
- rollback to stable image (in progress)
- scale up stable pool if qps spike (standby)
- route 10% traffic to us-west-2 stable pool (in progress)
- update status page if customer-visible (waiting on impact assessment)
Danielle Chen: Status page draft prepared, waiting on confirmed customer list from support. will push update after 15m once we see 5xx trending down.
oncall-monitor-bot: rollback finished on 6 pods, 12 remaining reinitializing. 5xx rate dropped to 3.1% over 3m
Miguel Soto: good. Priya, can you run smoke check script and paste results? 
Priya Narayanan: running smoke. 
```
./scripts/smoke-test --endpoint us-east-1 /v1/generate --n 20
```
Results: 19/20 successful, 1 timed out (~300ms). p95 latency 180ms.
Miguel Soto: acceptable. I'm going to prepare handoff notes. primary: Miguel (until 15:30 UTC) — secondary: Priya. coverage gap: none nominal but if errors climb above 5% escalate to SRE director.
Danielle Chen: filed ticket TKT-4921 with impact: 42 customers had transient errors, 7 customers reported degraded latency. tagged for retro and assigned to Priya for root cause analysis.
Miguel Soto: scheduling postmortem: tentative retro Wednesday 14:00 UTC in #postmortems. Danielle, can you create calendar invite and invite the deploy owner, SRE, oncall rotation leads, and infra eng?
Danielle Chen: invite sent to: Priya, Miguel, Kiran (deploy), Aisha (infra), SRE leads. Calendar event: Wed 14:00 UTC, Postmortem TKT-4921.
Priya Narayanan: initial RCA notes: kernel patch introduced an allocator change causing increased memory during cold start; under heavy concurrency this caused pods to OOM during model loading. mitigation: revert patch and add canary health gating with memory profiling. action items: see below.
Miguel Soto: recording action items here for handoff (short form): 
- ACTION-1: Priya -> Add memory profiling to canary pipeline + gate (due EOD tomorrow)
- ACTION-2: Kiran -> Improve deploy checklist to include 'model cold-start memory' tests (due next sprint)
- ACTION-3: Danielle -> Postmortem doc + customer impact table in TKT-4921 (due EOD today)
- ACTION-4: SRE -> Add automated rollback on >3 pods CrashLoop within 10min threshold (due next week)
Danielle Chen: adding those to TKT-4921. Also tagging customer success to prepare outreach templates.
Miguel Soto: handoff summary to next shift: rollback completed, currently monitoring; 5xx at ~2.5% trending down; tickets created: TKT-4921; retro scheduled; primary/secondary for remainder of my shift noted. If 5xx >5% for 10 minutes, escalate to SRE director and open Sev-2 bridge.
Priya Narayanan: noted. I'll monitor logs and escalate if we see repeated OOM stack traces. link to logs: https://logs.redwood/us-east-1/ded-ml-pool?from=2034567000
oncall-monitor-bot: Current summary — ded-ml-pool: 22/24 pods Ready, 2 CrashLoopBackOff; 5xx = 2.1% over 5m; routing rule active (10% to us-west-2).
Miguel Soto: ok wrapping up my watch. leaving oncall notes in the shift board. If anything flares, @Priya Narayanan is secondary.
Priya Narayanan: thanks. noted handoff. I'll pick this up if anything crops up.
Miguel Soto: handoff complete. :white_check_mark: 
Danielle Chen: closing loop — TKT-4921 updated with action items and retro invite. will ping when postmortem doc is ready for comment. :memo:
